elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall ...".

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: (a) "at Client's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: (b) "within thirty (30) days, return all Client Content and other Client data", running from the opening trigger of expiry or termination.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: (c) "after such return, delete such Client Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing".

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same opening trigger: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Up to six (6) months of transition assistance exceeds the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: (b) requires return of all Client Content and other Client data within thirty (30) days in machine-readable format.

reasons: The single inserted paragraph in the termination section covers all six preferred elements: trigger on expiry or termination, up to six months assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return of Client data in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion after return.

Insertion is concise and tracks the model language without extras: no survival tail, no at-own-expense wording, no added procedures or damages categories; it uses the document's existing defined term "Client Content" plus "other Client data" because the agreement has no "Customer Data" definition.

Existing favourable language is retained: Section 13's Client ownership of domains and Client Content and the 30/60-day arrangement duties, and Section 14's continuation of services, remain intact and do not contradict the new vendor-side return/deletion obligations (deletion is expressly post-return, avoiding walk-away immediate deletion).
No dangling cross-references or undefined triggers are introduced; timing runs from expiry or termination as the checklist requires.
